classified_spans.text:
## Novel Step

The invention introduces an evaluation graph decomposition engine that automatically breaks complex enterprise agent tasks into a directed acyclic graph of subtasks, classifying each node as deterministically verifiable or subjectively assessable, then routes each node to the appropriate evaluation mechanism. This matters because existing agent evaluation approaches treat the entire task as a single unit, forcing evaluators to choose between automated metrics that miss nuance and human review that does not scale. By operating at the subtask level and combining heterogeneous evaluation signals through a weighted confidence aggregation layer, the framework produces repeatable, auditable scores for agent workflows that span both structured operations and open-ended reasoning.

## How It Works

The framework begins with a task specification ingestion layer that accepts enterprise objectives in natural language, structured YAML, or a combination of both. When a new evaluation request arrives, the decomposition engine parses the objective and emits an evaluation graph: a DAG where each node represents a discrete subtask and edges capture data dependencies between them. The engine uses a combination of static analysis (detecting references to APIs, databases, or code artifacts) and an LLM-based classifier to label each node with an evaluation type. Nodes involving tool calls, API responses, SQL queries, or code execution receive a "deterministic" label; nodes involving summarization quality, strategic reasoning, or tone receive a "subjective" label. This classification step also attaches metadata such as expected output schemas, tolerance thresholds, and domain tags that downstream evaluators will consume.

Deterministic nodes flow into an automated verification runtime built on Open Policy Agent (OPA) and a custom assertion library. For each node, the runtime pulls the agent's actual output artifact, whether that is an HTTP response, a generated SQL result set, or a file diff, and runs it against the expected output specification. Assertions can be exact match, schema conformance, range checks, or semantic equivalence via embedding similarity with a configurable cosine threshold. The runtime produces a binary pass/fail verdict along with a granular mismatch report for any failures. Because these checks are fully automated, the framework can evaluate thousands of deterministic subtasks per minute without human involvement.

Subjective nodes follow a different path. The framework maintains a pool of evaluation channels: calibrated LLM judges, human reviewers accessible through a review queue API, and hybrid panels that combine both. A routing policy, expressed as a Rego rule set, determines which channel handles each subjective node based on factors like domain sensitivity, required expertise, and cost budget. LLM judges operate as structured graders: they receive the subtask output, a rubric generated from the evaluation graph metadata, and a set of calibration anchors (reference outputs with known scores). Human reviewers see the same rubric through a web interface and submit Likert-scale ratings plus free-text justifications. To keep LLM judges honest, the framework periodically injects "canary" items with known human scores and flags any judge whose agreement with the canary set drops below a configurable kappa threshold.

Once all nodes in the evaluation graph have verdicts, the confidence aggregation layer walks the DAG bottom-up. Each node's score is a float between 0.0 and 1.0. Deterministic nodes map pass/fail to 1.0/0.0 unless partial credit rules apply. Subjective nodes normalize their ratings to the same range. The aggregation layer applies learned weights to each node based on its domain tag and historical importance, then propagates scores upward through the graph using a weighted geometric mean at each merge point. The root node's final value becomes the unified confidence score for the entire agent task. The framework also computes a decomposition coverage metric that flags any portion of the original objective that the engine could not map to a subtask node, ensuring evaluators know when the graph is incomplete.

All evaluation artifacts, including the graph structure, per-node verdicts, raw evaluator responses, and the final score, are persisted in an evaluation ledger backed by PostgreSQL. A feedback compiler reads the ledger after each evaluation run and generates structured improvement signals: which subtasks failed, what the failure mode was, and a suggested remediation category (prompt refinement, tool configuration, retrieval tuning, or model upgrade). These signals can be consumed by agent training pipelines or surfaced to operations teams through a Grafana dashboard. Over successive runs, the framework also refines its own decomposition heuristics and node weights using the accumulated ledger data, making the evaluation itself more accurate over time.

## Enablement Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: eval-framework-config
  namespace: agent-evaluation
data:
  decomposition.yaml: |
    engine:
      classifier_model: "granite-3.2-8b"
      classifier_confidence_floor: 0.85
      fallback_label: "subjective"
    node_types:
      deterministic:
        evaluator: "opa-assertion-runtime"
        embedding_similarity_threshold: 0.92
        partial_credit: false
      subjective:
        default_channel: "llm-judge"
        llm_judge_model: "granite-3.2-8b"
        canary_injection_rate: 0.10
        kappa_alert_threshold: 0.65
        human_fallback_on_low_kappa: true

  routing-policy.rego: |
    package eval.routing

    default channel = "llm-judge"

    channel = "human-review" {
      input.node.domain_tag == "compliance"
    }

    channel = "human-review" {
      input.node.sensitivity >= 0.9
    }

    channel = "hybrid-panel" {
      input.node.domain_tag == "strategy"
      input.cost_budget_remaining > 50
    }

  aggregation.yaml: |
    strategy: "weighted-geometric-mean"
    weight_source: "learned"
    weight_fallback:
      deterministic: 1.0
      subjective: 0.8
    coverage_warning_threshold: 0.90
    score_output:
      precision: 4
      include_per_node_breakdown: true

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: eval-decomposition-engine
  namespace: agent-evaluation
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: decomposition-engine
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: decomposition-engine
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: engine
          image: registry.redhat.io/agent-eval/decomposition-engine:1.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: eval-framework-config
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: "2Gi"
              cpu: "1000m"
            limits:
              memory: "4Gi"
              cpu: "2000m"

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: opa-assertion-runtime
  namespace: agent-evaluation
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: opa-assertion-runtime
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: opa-assertion-runtime
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: opa
          image: registry.redhat.io/agent-eval/opa-assertion:1.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8181
          volumeMounts:
            - name: policy-volume
              mountPath: /policies
      volumes:
        - name: policy-volume
          configMap:
            name: eval-framework-config
            items:
              - key: routing-policy.rego
                path: routing.rego

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: confidence-aggregator
  namespace: agent-evaluation
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: confidence-aggregator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: confidence-aggregator
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: aggregator
          image: registry.redhat.io/agent-eval/confidence-aggregator:1.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8082
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: eval-framework-config
```

This configuration deploys the three core services of the evaluation framework into a dedicated `agent-evaluation` namespace. The ConfigMap bundles all tunable parameters into a single resource. The `decomposition.yaml` section controls the classifier model used for labeling subtask nodes, sets the confidence floor below which the engine falls back to the "subjective" label, and configures per-type evaluator settings including the embedding similarity threshold for deterministic checks and the canary injection rate for LLM judge calibration. The `routing-policy.rego` file is a live OPA policy that the assertion runtime and the subjective evaluation router both consume; it encodes organizational rules such as routing all compliance-tagged nodes to human reviewers and sending strategy nodes to a hybrid panel when budget permits. The `aggregation.yaml` section tells the confidence aggregator to use the weighted geometric mean strategy with learned weights pulled from the evaluation ledger, falling back to static defaults (1.0 for deterministic, 0.8 for subjective) when insufficient historical data exists. The decomposition engine deployment runs two replicas behind a cluster service, accepting task specifications over HTTP and emitting evaluation graphs serialized as JSON DAGs. The OPA assertion runtime scales to three replicas to handle burst evaluation of deterministic nodes, mounting the Rego policy from the ConfigMap so policy changes propagate without redeployment. The confidence aggregator reads completed node verdicts from the evaluation ledger, computes the unified score, and writes the final result back alongside the per-node breakdown for downstream consumption by training pipelines or observability dashboards.

# Invention Idea
